Superionicity and premelting of iron-rich (Fe,Mg)O at Earth’s core-mantle boundary
articles.abstract: Abstract Core-mantle interactions are essential for understanding Earth’s interior dynamics and evolution. Experimental studies reveal that core-mantle reactions produce iron-rich (Fe,Mg)O (periclase‑wüstite solid solution). Here we show that Fe-rich (Fe,Mg)O exhibits pronounced superionic-onset and grain-boundary premelting behavior above ~0.9 T m ( T m : melting temperature). These effects are significant in (Fe x Mg 1-x )O (x > 0.8) under core-mantle boundary (CMB) conditions, causing elastic softening, enhanced elemental transport, and ultra-low viscosity. Enhanced diffusion may facilitate core-mantle reactions and the accumulation of Fe-rich material near the CMB, potentially contributing to a dense basal assemblage. Under mantle flow and/or thermal buoyancy, the low viscosity of connected Fe-rich (Fe,Mg)O could favor deformation and redistribution toward shallower depths. This process may contribute to the formation and evolution of some ultra-low velocity zones (ULVZs). The proposed scenario is consistent with the layered structures and inferred low viscosity of some ULVZs and suggests a potential role for Fe-rich (Fe,Mg)O in core-mantle material exchange and heat transfer.

articles.title: Boosting Sensitivity of High-Dimensional Solid-State NMR of Proteins by Optimizing Coherence Transfers
articles.abstract: Abstract TROP it or drop it: Owing to fast magic-angle spinning at frequencies above 50 kHz, solid-state nuclear magnetic resonance has evolved as a versatile method to decipher protein structure, dynamics, and chemical properties. While conceptually, higher-dimensional approaches such as 4D and 5D correlation spectra are capable of exceeding the established molecular-weight limitations by ameliorating signal overlap, their intrinsic implications for sensitivity and measurement times required have severely limited these important prospects in practice. Here we show that in high-dimensional experiments, the extensive use of dedicated transverse-mixing optimal control pulses (TROPs) can reduce the necessary measurement time by almost an order of magnitude. TROP’ed non-uniformly sampled experiments not only benefit from a multiplicative sensitivity enhancement in each complex time point due to concomitant transfer of both components of complex signals along multi-step magnetization transfer pathways, but additionally from facilitation of reconstruction with better raw data. Aided by the processing framework provided to future users here, the combination of an extensive use of TROPs with increased dimensionality hence presents itself as highly promising to ameliorate the conventional limitations of solid-state NMR.

articles.title: VapC40 diverts autophagic flux from xenophagy to mitophagy via ammonia-dependent metabolic toxicity
Low-temperature operation of Ag—C based anodeless all-solid-state pouch cells
articles.abstract: Abstract Anodeless all-solid-state batteries with Ag-C interlayers offer high energy density and long cycle life, yet their operation in cold environments remains limited by poorly understood failure mechanisms. Using operando X-ray absorption spectroscopy, cryogenic-cross-section electron microscopy, and X-ray diffraction, we discover that Li-Ag alloying dynamics are highly temperature-dependent: rapid at 45 °C but kinetically suppressed at 5 °C. At low temperatures, suppressed alloying leads to sluggish lithium transport, internal lithium extrusion, interlayer delamination, and rapid capacity decay. We demonstrate that a brief initial charge at 45 °C permanently activates the interlayer via Li-Ag alloy formation, enabling efficient Li transport even at 5 °C. Full pouch cells following this activation protocol retain 87% of their initial capacity after 250 completed cycles following one formation cycle at 5 °C. After 250 cycles at 5 °C, AAP-treated cells delivered approximately three times the discharge capacity of cells cycled with the fixed-temperature protocol. Such in situ electrochemical alloy activation offers a practical and scalable approach to extend anodeless all-solid-state battery performance to sub-ambient temperatures without material redesign.

articles.title: Lysine-R2HGylation-C5 identified as a post-translational modification in R2HG-elevated cancers
An ingestible, bio-inspired self-powered electrocapsule for in situ ethanol clearance mitigates systemic and neurobehavioral toxicity
Bicontinuous Fibre Formation via Co-precipitate Attenuated Solvent Transfer Induced Assembly
articles.abstract: Abstract Polymer–solvent–nonsolvent mixtures provide a versatile route for fabricating structured materials through liquid–liquid phase separation. In this context, solvent transfer–induced phase separation (STrIPS) enables the continuous formation of bicontinuous fibres, yet the process is often limited by coarsening of pores or collapse within the fibre core, leading to structural inhomogeneity. Here, we advance this strategy through Co-precipitate Attenuated Solvent Transfer induced assembly (CAST), in which amphiphilic species precipitate in situ during solvent exchange and preferentially retained within the polymer rich phase. These precipitates act as a distributed molecular retarding agent that delays domain growth, thereby preserving bicontinuity throughout the fibre cross-section to up to 250 µm. Using a poly (ethylene glycol) diacrylate–ethanol–water system with a phenolic oligomer coprecipitate, we demonstrate that CAST stabilizes the hollow bicontinuous domain structure, extending the attainable specific surface area by ca. 100%. Scattering experiments and molecular dynamics simulations confirm that the precipitating species suppress coarsening by restricting mobility within the phase they occupy. Embedding CAST fibres within polydimethylsiloxane demonstrates lightweight composites with sound mitigation capabilities, highlighting the potential for acoustic applications. CAST thus establishes a versatile route to high-performance porous materials with broad potential for structural, acoustic, and energy applications.

articles.title: Bioenergetic responses to β-adrenergic stimulation in beige adipocytes depend on actomyosin driven forces
articles.abstract: Abstract Beige and white adipocytes reside within the same fat depots but differ in their responses to β-adrenergic stimulation. While both activate classical protein kinase A (PKA)-mediated pathways, only beige adipocytes show induction of uncoupling protein 1 (UCP1) expression and enhanced mitochondrial respiration, suggesting additional mechanisms that distinguish their responses. Here we uncover a parallel, non-canonical biomechanical pathway specific to committed beige adipocytes that is required for the full β-adrenergic induction of their thermogenic activity. Mechanistically, β-adrenergic receptor (β-AR) stimulation induces a rapid myosin heavy chain 9 (Myh9)-mediated actomyosin contraction and stiffening in differentiated beige but not white adipocytes that activates focal adhesion kinase (FAK), which we show to be critical for the expression of oxidative and thermogenic genes including UCP1 and perilipin 5 (PLIN5). These findings reveal an alternative biomechanical Myh9-FAK signaling arm downstream of β-adrenergic activation that distinguishes thermogenic beige adipocytes from white adipocytes.

articles.title: A spatiotemporal scaffold in the human subiculum supports episodic memory and its enhancement through navigation training
Dual-functional-unit modulation enables superior energy storage in high-entropy relaxor ferroelectrics
A revised genome annotation of the model cyanobacterium Synechocystis based on start and stop codon-enriched ribosome profiling and proteogenomics
articles.abstract: Abstract Cyanobacteria are important primary producers and popular in biotechnology. Synechocystis 6803 is a model cyanobacterium, yet many coding regions are ambiguous, or have remained undetected. Here, we present a riboproteogenomic analysis combining ribosome profiling with inhibitors that stall ribosomes at translation initiation and termination sites, and proteogenomic re-annotation of its genome. Based on proteogenomics, we report translation of 3055 annotated genes (83%), 3492 based on Ribo-seq (95.2%), and 3,018 supported by both methods (82%). The data suggest additional protein-coding genes and corrections for annotated ones. We validate 15 proteins translated from antisense, intergenic and intragenic loci and provide proteogenomic support for up to 69 additional, mostly small proteins. We identify three genes with ~300 nt long intragenic out-of-frame translons and demonstrate that internal and host translons are translated into interacting proteins. Our data are accessible at https://www.bioinf.uni-freiburg.de/~ribobase/ . They illustrate the enormous value of consolidating genome annotations with integrated experimental data.

articles.title: Quantum-accurate vibrational and conformational dynamics from small molecules to proteins with machine-learned force fields
articles.abstract: Abstract Biomolecular thermodynamics and spectroscopy depend on relative conformer energies, local curvatures, and collective dipole fluctuations on the potential-energy surface. Conventional molecular mechanics force fields enable large-scale simulations, but their fixed functional forms can misrepresent infrared intensities, mode character, and environment-dependent vibrational response. Here we assess general-purpose machine-learned force fields by using finite-temperature infrared spectra across small molecules, gas-phase peptides, and monomeric, oligomeric, and solvated protein assemblies. To enable this analysis, we introduce QVib, a dataset of 293 molecules and 1366 conformers, together with peptide amide-band benchmarks and p53 oligomerization-domain models, to evaluate vibrational transferability from DFT references to experimental spectra. Across these systems, machine-learned force fields improve over molecular mechanics in reproducing DFT-level forces, vibrational frequencies, densities of states, mode eigenvectors, conformational energetics, and experimental infrared spectra. Among models with explicit long-range electrostatics, SO3LR provides the best accuracy–cost balance of the models tested here. These results show that machine-learned force-field dynamics can recover collective, environment-dependent vibrational landscapes at near-DFT fidelity, enabling spectroscopically validated biomolecular simulations at force-field-like cost.

articles.title: A master gene for Drosophila male courtship prevents the behavior in females via a truncated protein
4D printing of multi-state pH-responsive microstructures
articles.abstract: Abstract Deep eutectic systems (DESs) are emerging as highly versatile functional materials for 3D printing, particularly in multiphoton 3D laser printing (MPLP), a powerful technique for the fabrication of complex microstructures with high spatial resolution. Here, we present a versatile strategy for the fabrication of multi-state pH-responsive microactuators based on polymerizable DESs using MPLP. By incorporating vinyl phosphonic acid and vinyl imidazole as functional monomers, respectively, we establish two actively responsive DESs that exhibit antagonistic swelling behavior across the pH range while maintaining excellent printability. The printed 3D microstructures show pronounced and reversible pH-responsive actuation with high cycling stability. Combining both materials within single architectures enables multi-state and bidirectional actuation beyond conventional bilayer systems. Complex actuator geometries further demonstrate the versatility of the platform. A hyperelastic theory implemented in a finite element framework can predict the experimentally observed actuation patterns. These results highlight the potential of polymerizable DESs as a new material platform for advanced microscale soft robotic, sensing, and adaptive systems.

articles.title: Supervised deep learning for efficient cryo-EM image alignment in drug discovery with cryoPARES
Impact of Comorbid Depression and Anxiety on the Mortality among Adults with Cardiometabolic Diseases

Internal
Molecular Response Chains to Inhaled Volatile
Organic Compounds for Precision Health Risk Assessment Revealed by
Breathomics
articles.abstract: Abstract Volatile organic compounds (VOCs) are airborne pollutants, yet risk assessment based solely on external concentrations may miss internal molecular effects under low-level mixture exposure. We collected exhaled breath and ambient air samples from 67 child volunteers for VOC profiling, with blood samples from 16 participants used for transcriptomic and metabolomic analyses. A physiological compartment-based kinetic model identified 76 endogenous and 44 exogenous VOCs in breath, and dimensionality reduction grouped exogenous VOCs into seven chemically interpretable exposure patterns. These patterns were associated with 86 genes involving cell cycle and neural pathways and nominally with 247 metabolites, suggesting potential variation in energy, lipid and amino acid metabolism, and neurotransmitter homeostasis. Multiomics integration further suggested seven endogenous VOCs as candidate signals reflecting variation across exposure, transcriptome, and metabolome layers. Benzothiazole, 3,7-dimethyl-nonane, and 2-methyl-2-propenoic acid were associated with both conventional cancer risk estimates and cancer pathway activity, whereas conventional cancer risk showed only weak correlation with this internal phenotype. These findings support an internal molecular response framework connecting inhaled VOC exposure to biological effects and highlight the potential of breathomics for precision health risk assessment.

articles.title:
Environmentally
Relevant F-53B Exposure Triggers
Ovarian Cancer Progression via C5aR1-Mediated Noncanonical Signaling:
An Adverse Outcome Pathway (AOP) Underlying Hybrid EMT and Stemness
articles.abstract: Abstract Significant gaps remain in the health risk assessment methodologies for the PFOS (perfluorooctanesulfonic acid) alternative 6:2 Cl-PFESA (6:2 chlorinated polyfluoroalkyl ether sulfonate, F-53B), which has been widely recognized as the alternative to PFOS in China. To address this research gap, our study integrated multidimensional techniques to mechanistically construct an Adverse Outcome Pathway (AOP) for F-53B-induced ovarian cancer progression. Our findings demonstrated that exposure to environmentally relevant concentrations of F-53B significantly enhanced the migratory and invasive capabilities of ovarian cancer cells. Within the AOP framework of F-53B-induced hybrid epithelial-mesenchymal transition (EMT) and enhanced tumor stemness, the upregulation of C5aR1─triggered by ERα acting as a noncanonical receptor of F-53B─constitutes the molecular initiating event (MIE). Following this MIE, the recruitment of β-arrestin1 and Src was induced, leading to the assembly of a C5aR1/β-arrestin1/Src signaling complex. This complex facilitated the binding of β-arrestin1 to β-catenin and drove the nuclear translocation of β-catenin, ultimately activating hybrid EMT and stemness of tumor cells. Administration of the C5aR1 inhibitor PMX205 effectively abrogated subsequent key events (KEs) caused by F-53B exposure. Through in vitro and in vivo validation, our study established an AOP framework that provides a novel perspective for evaluating the potential risk of PFAS substitutes in promoting cancer progression.

articles.title:
Continuous and Episodic
Metal Exposures Disrupt Aquatic
Insect Drift, Emergence, and Larval Survival
articles.abstract: Abstract Metal contamination in streams occurs under both chronic and episodic exposures, yet the effects of varying exposure on invertebrate life-history processes are poorly understood. We conducted two 9-day mesocosm experiments with benthic macroinvertebrate communities to compare the effects of continuous and pulsed exposures to dissolved copper and zinc on larval drift, adult emergence, and benthic survival. Our goal was to evaluate how different exposure regimes alter in situ survival relative to the downstream movement of invertebrate prey resources and their dispersal to terrestrial consumers. Both exposure regimes significantly increased total larval drift (29–52% above controls), with Baetidae (Ephemeroptera) and Hydropsychidae (Trichoptera) dominating the drift response. Cumulative daily drift increased rapidly after initial exposure, with Baetidae under continuous exposure showing 3-fold higher drift relative to controls. Total emergence was higher under continuous exposure and was primarily driven by stimulated emergence in Chironomidae (Diptera). Total benthic abundance declined by 24–33% across treatments and was similar between exposure regimes, suggesting responses were more strongly associated with peak concentrations than cumulative dose. Together, our results show that continuous and episodic metal exposures can reduce benthic abundance while simultaneously increasing emigration through drift and emergence, thereby altering critical ecosystem services provided by aquatic insects.

articles.title:
Screening Environmental
Toxicants for Neurodevelopmental
Disorders Using a hPSC-Based Mitochondrial Redox Biosensor
articles.abstract: Abstract Environmental chemical exposure during prenatal development significantly elevates the risk of neurodevelopmental disorders (NDDs), with mitochondrial oxidative stress representing a central convergent mechanism. However, existing screening platforms lack the genetic stability and developmental stage specificity required for systematic identification of neurotoxic hazards across human neural lineage progression. Here, we established a human pluripotent stem cell (hPSC)-based mitochondrial redox biosensor by CRISPR/Cas9-mediated targeted integration of the genetically encoded H2O2 probe mito-HyPer7 into the AAVS1 safe-harbor locus, ensuring stable expression across pluripotent, neurogenic, and neuronal stages. Using this platform, we screened 76 epidemiologically relevant industrial chemicals and identified reactive oxygen species-inducing toxicants (ROS-ITs) with lineage-stage-selective profiles across neural lineages. Neural progenitor cells (NPCs) exhibited the broadest sensitivity spectrum, revealing neurogenesis as a critical developmental window. Among the screened compounds, bisphenol G (BPG)─an emerging alternative in plastic production─displayed cross-stage toxicity surpassing that of bisphenol A (BPA). In three-dimensional cortical organoids, BPG impaired radial glial cell (RGC) proliferation, triggered precocious neurogenic transition, and induced apoptosis, culminating in disrupted cortical architecture. Mechanistically, BPG aberrantly activated thyroid hormone receptor (TR)-mediated transcription, and the resulting developmental impairment was partially ameliorated by the receptor antagonist NH-3. Collectively, this study presents an integrative framework that unites a genetically stable platform for high-throughput mitochondrial redox screening with organoid-based pathological and mechanistic validation, providing a comprehensive paradigm for identifying and characterizing environmental toxicants that threaten human neurodevelopment.

articles.title:
Can
Small Modular Reactors Enable State-Specific Energy
Portfolios for US AI Ambitions through 2035?
articles.abstract: Abstract The rapid expansion of AI infrastructure in the US is emerging as a major new source of electricity demand, raising concerns about fossil lock-in during accelerated grid expansion. Here, we assess the role of small modular reactors (SMRs) within portfolios that also include on-site solar and wind power, grid electricity, battery storage, and direct air capture. Using a state-resolved scenario analysis for 2028–2035, we compare nuclear-inclusive and non-nuclear portfolios across alternative AI load trajectories, SSP-RCP electricity mixes, and decarbonization constraints. Relative to a grid-only counterfactual, nuclear-inclusive portfolios that achieve carbon neutrality by 2035 require 2.4–47.2 GW of SMR capacity, avoid 0.3–1.3 GtCO2, reduce water consumption by an amount equivalent to the annual use of 28.3–50.5 million people, and deliver \$105.8–194.8 billion in cumulative energy-system cost savings across climate and efficiency pathways. The results show that SMRs can materially expand cost-effective decarbonization options for AI infrastructure, while their contribution depends on timely deployment, permitting, and coordination with state-level electricity planning.

articles.title:
Dust
Storms as Dynamic Multipollutant Exposure Systems:
Environmental Transformation, Toxicological Mechanisms, and Health
Implications
articles.abstract: Abstract Dust particles have long been considered to be naturally derived mineral particles. However, with the increase in regional anthropogenic emissions and atmospheric multipollutant processes, their environmental significance as pollutant carriers and multicomponent exposure media has increasingly attracted attention. Nevertheless, existing studies have primarily focused on dust event characteristics, variations in particulate matter concentrations, or the effects of individual pollutant components, while a systematic understanding of the formation processes and health implications of dust as a dynamic multipollutant exposure system remains limited. This review conceptualizes dust storms as a dynamic multipollutant exposure system and integrates evidence from environmental chemistry, exposure science, toxicology, and epidemiology to discuss the environmental behavior of dust-associated pollutant components, their potential mechanisms of action, and their associations with population health effects. This review aims to advance the understanding of the processes underlying health risks associated with dust storms and provide a scientific basis for the development of future dust-related health risk assessment frameworks.

articles.title:
Cross-Domain
Tracing of Rice Stem Stress under Soil
Cadmium Pollution
articles.abstract: Abstract Plants exposed to heavy-metal-contaminated soil are subjected to pollutant pressure, making timely monitoring of plant condition important for assessing their responses to soil pollution. Although spectral sensing is widely used for nondestructive monitoring of plant stress, the cross-domain association between plant optical signals and Cd-induced physiological responses remains unclear. Here, we integrated spectral sensing with deep learning, Monte Carlo simulation, and omics analysis to systematically explore how spectral signals and physiological responses jointly support the monitoring of Cd-induced stress in rice stems. We found that Cd exposure reorganized interface-associated stress, protective chemistry, and redox regulation into coordinated Defense, Repair, and Adjustment signatures. These biological changes were differentially expressed across the visible, red-edge, and near-infrared spectral regions, producing a reweighting of absorption- and scattering-sensitive information. The agreement between spectral variation and biological stress signatures further established a cross-domain link between stress-state formation and optical detection. Benefiting from this mechanism, we achieved high-accuracy nondestructive detection of rice stem Cd content and noninvasive characterization of Cd-induced responses. A portable spectrometer–smartphone implementation further demonstrated field-oriented feasibility. These findings provide a biological and optical basis for tracking stress progression and supporting timely, feedback-guided crop management.

articles.title:
Air–Water
Interfacial Secondary Hydroxylation
of SO2: An Overlooked and Rapid Pathway to Sulfuric Acid
in Tropical Coastal Industrial Areas
articles.abstract: Abstract Atmospheric sulfuric acid (H2SO4) is a key driver of acid deposition, aerosol growth, and new particle formation. Its formation is initiated by rapid OH addition to SO2 to produce HOSO2, but direct hydroxylation of HOSO2 is kinetically unfavorable. Consequently, the accepted route to H2SO4 proceeds via O2 oxidation of HOSO2 to SO3, followed by hydrolysis. Here, using classical molecular dynamics (MD) and Born–Oppenheimer MD simulations, we identify an alternative interfacial pathway that directly converts HOSO2 and OH into H2SO4. Strong interfacial affinity of both reactants drives this transformation at the air–water interface with a free-energy barrier of only 1.73 kcal·mol–1, substantially lower than that of gas-phase SO3 hydrolysis. Kinetic analysis further indicates that, under conditions of elevated OH, HOSO2, and low SO3, this pathway can outpace gas-phase SO3 hydrolysis by more than 3 orders of magnitude. These results reveal an efficient interfacial source of atmospheric H2SO4, offering a mechanistic basis for its elevated abundance in polluted coastal environments and improving the representation of sulfur oxidation in atmospheric models.

articles.title:
Landfills Act as
Persistent Reservoirs of Rubber-Derived
Chemicals, Driving Widespread Subsurface Migration and Groundwater
Contamination
articles.abstract: Abstract Rubber-derived chemicals (RDCs) are emerging contaminants of concern in various environments, yet their occurrence, migration, and ecological risks in landfill and groundwater remain insufficiently understood. In this study, 35 RDCs were investigated in landfill leachate and groundwater from three municipal landfills, covering raw and treated leachate as well as upstream, on-site, and downstream groundwater across wet and dry seasons. Results showed widespread detection of RDCs in all matrices, with benzothiazoles and other RDCs reaching peak levels of 85890 ng/L, substantially exceeding p-phenylenediamines (PPDs, 869 ng/L) and their quinones (PPD-Qs, 443 ng/L). Although conventional treatment reduced total RDC levels, most compounds remained detectable in effluents (1.10–4946 ng/L). Groundwater analyses revealed clear spatial gradients, with on-site aquifers showing the highest contamination, while downstream groundwater still exhibited significantly elevated concentrations and compositional similarity to landfill leachate, implying subsurface migration. Seasonal variation was observed only in on-site groundwater, indicating that landfill systems amplify climatic effects on contaminant behavior. Risk assessment further indicated that PPD-Qs and 1,3-diphenylguanidine (DPG) were primary contributors to ecological risk in both leachate and groundwater (RQ far above 1). Overall, landfill systems act as persistent sources and subsurface conduits of RDCs, posing long-term risks to surrounding groundwater environments.

articles.title:
Broad Nuclear Receptor-Binding
Activities of Phase
II Sulfate Metabolites Revealed by the Combinatorial Synthesis for
Environmental Research (CoSyER) Approach with Affinity Selection Mass
Spectrometry (ASMS)
articles.abstract: Abstract Biotransformation alters the bioactivity of xenobiotics in humans; however, traditional approaches are infeasible for testing large numbers of metabolites. Herein, we propose a high-throughput combinatorial synthesis for environmental research and a protein affinity selection mass spectrometry approach (CoSyER:ASMS) for assessing the receptor-binding activities of hundreds of metabolites within weeks. As proof of concept, 132 sulfate metabolites were synthesized from 222 ToxCast chemicals using an optimized one-pot combinatorial synthesis approach. Four nuclear receptors (PPARγ, PXR, ERRγ, and FXR) were further selected for AS-MS analysis to evaluate the binding activities of 132 sulfate metabolites and corresponding parent compounds, covering 1056 binary interactions. Interestingly, sulfate metabolites exhibited broad nuclear receptor-binding activities toward PPARγ and PXR, with 29 and 24 ligands detected by AS-MS, respectively. Bioactivities and functional effects of triclosan sulfate and 1-hydroxypyrene sulfate were validated by orthogonal fluorescence assay and human cell receptor assays. Collectively, this study introduces CoSyER:ASMS as a scalable platform integrating high-throughput generation of sulfate metabolites with receptor-binding screening to accelerate the toxicological prioritization of this understudied metabolite class.

articles.title:
Forensic Accounting
of Kelp Carbon Sequestration:
Geomorphic and Microbial Controls on Permanence and Verifiability
articles.abstract: Abstract Kelp forests fix substantial amounts of carbon, but the fraction reaching long-term storage remains unclear. This review uses forensic accounting to assess evidence for kelp carbon sequestration, focusing on geomorphic and microbial controls on permanence and verifiability. Studies show kelp production and export, while retention estimates depend on the receiving environment and assessment period. Kelp-derived particulate carbon has been detected in deep water and sediments, whereas the long-term fate of kelp-derived dissolved organic carbon (DOC) remains poorly quantified. Geomorphology affects transport distance, source–sink connectivity, and access to depositional environments. Microbial processing controls degradation and remineralization and can generate recalcitrant DOC through the microbial carbon pump (MCP). Short transport pathways and slower degradation can increase particulate delivery, but retention also depends on circulation, ventilation, and postdepositional loss. For carbon remineralized to dissolved inorganic carbon (DIC), storage duration depends on remineralization depth and water-mass ventilation. Persistent DOC storage estimates require source attribution, pool size, and residence time. We link each carbon claim to measurements in the receiving reservoir and distinguish marine carbon storage from net atmospheric CO2 removal and project-level crediting. Integrating source attribution, transport, microbial transformation, and reservoir retention can improve storage estimates and guide monitoring.

articles.title: Transforming spinel LiMn2O4 into a Na-layered cathode
articles.abstract: Abstract The positive electrode structures of practical sodium-ion batteries are generally confined to polyanionic or layered transition metal oxide frameworks, where the trade-off between specific energy and structural stability limits their application. As a well-established positive electrode structure in lithium-ion batteries, the spinel framework has abundant storage sites for alkali metal ions, but it has received less attention for sodium-ion batteries. Here we show that spinel LiMn 2 O 4 can be transformed into a sodium-ion positive electrode. Electrochemical sodiation drives Mn-ion migration along an octahedral–tetrahedral–octahedral pathway, creating a layered/spinel heterostructure for further sodium storage. Moreover, residual spinel domains inhibit the strain and structural degradation within the layered structure. Consequently, a 26650 cylindrical cell using a LiMn 2 O 4 -derived sodium-ion positive electrode achieves a capacity of 3.85 Ah and retains 95.7% capacity after 900 cycles (1.925 A). This work demonstrates that spinel LiMn 2 O 4 can serve as a viable positive electrode for sodium-ion batteries, and that electrochemical transformation is a feasible approach for creating positive electrode frameworks.

articles.title: Focused ultrasound neuromodulation of mediodorsal thalamus disrupts decision flexibility during reward learning
articles.abstract: Abstract When learning to find the most beneficial course of action, the prefrontal cortex guides decisions by comparing estimates of the relative value of the options available. Basic neuroscience studies in animals support the view that the thalamus can regulate this activity within and across the prefrontal cortex. We studied a group of patients (n = 37) undergoing unilateral MR-guided focused ultrasound for essential tremor, performing the restless bandit, a reward reinforcement learning task, immediately before and after thalamotomy. Thalamotomy significantly impaired the proportion of switch choices during the task without affecting overall performance. This effect was observed when the task was delivered to co-incide with maximal vasogenic thalamic oedema but not in a control group tested on the same day of their treatment. A reinforcement learning model fitted to the patients’ choices replicated the effect of thalamotomy when the model increased exploitation of the bandits’ learnt value estimate. This shift in the explore-exploit trade-off, manifesting as reduced choice flexibility, co-varied with the pattern of post-operative oedema extension into the mediodorsal nucleus. These findings confirm a causal role of the thalamus and specifically the mediodorsal nucleus in regulating the extent to which value estimates are used to guide decisions and learning from reward.

articles.title:
Developing Partial
Characterization Factors for Ship
Noise Impacts on Marine Biodiversity in European Seas
articles.abstract: Abstract Shipping is the primary source of underwater noise pollution, yet its impacts on marine biodiversity remain unquantified in Life Cycle Impact Assessment (LCIA). This study presents the first framework for quantifying the regionalized impact of ship noise on marine mammal biodiversity within LCIA, demonstrated for European Seas. Ship noise data from the NAVISON project for 2019 were combined with species-specific sensitivity thresholds for marine mammals to derive spatially explicit Potentially Affected Fractions (PAF). Partial characterization factors (pCFs) for 21 country groups were calculated by integrating PAF values with spatially explicit transport work and maritime trade data, ranging from zero to 1.00 × 10–14 PAF × yr × ton-km–1 (Northern Europe), with a mean of 1.86 × 10–15 PAF × yr × ton-km–1. The total impact of ship noise per country was calculated for 200 countries by multiplying the pCF with each country’s maritime trade. The United Kingdom has the highest total impact (1.34× 10–2 PAF × yr), followed by the United States of America and Spain. This framework represents a first step toward integrating ship noise as a novel impact category in LCIA, supporting comprehensive environmental assessments of global supply chains alongside other maritime stressors such as greenhouse gas emissions and marine invasive species.

articles.title: 60 Years of  ES&T  in Pursuit of Sustainable Systems
Issue Editorial Masthead
Issue Publication Information

Robust Dual-Cycle
Direct Air Capture Process Enabled
by a Novel Biphasic Solvent
articles.abstract: Abstract Traditional liquid-based DAC (L-DAC) technology suffers from high energy consumption and transportation difficulties due to complex intermediate conversion and oxidative degradation, despite its fast kinetics. To address these challenges, this study proposed a dual-cycle DAC strategy using a novel biphasic absorbent ([PZ][1,2,4]-NMP). Atmospheric CO2 was first captured by KOH and converted to K2CO3. Subsequently, under air-isolated conditions, [PZ][1,2,4] selectively displaced CO2 from K2CO3, concentrating it into a flowable carbamate slurry. By confining regeneration to this small-volume slurry, a low-energy penalty of 1.37–1.45 GJ·t–1CO2 was achieved. The closed-loop design effectively prevented oxidative degradation of the active components and significantly enhanced phase separation. This dual-cycle architecture provides a promising pathway for energy-efficient and operationally robust DAC technologies.

articles.title:
The Acute Exposure
Window: A Missing Dimension in
Industrial Fire Assessment

Developing Complementary
Aquatic Sentinel Panels for
Cross-Chemical Monitoring and Regional Localization
articles.abstract: Abstract Sparse and uneven multispecies toxicity data make it difficult to select a small panel of aquatic sentinels that includes sensitive species across priority chemicals. We developed COMPASS (Complementarity-Oriented Monitoring Panels of Aquatic Sentinel Species) to select complementary sentinel species using species sensitivity distributions (SSDs). Of 2,026 SSDs fitted within chemical and test-condition groups from 426,588 waterborne toxicity records, 1,613 with at least six species supported focal-species leave-one-out estimation; 413 five-species groups supported supplementary comparisons. The national top-5 comprised Gastrophryne carolinensis, Neocloeon triangulifer, Hyalella azteca, Daphnia ambigua, and Daphnia magna. Chemical-priority-weighted expected capture was 33.8%, 62.4%, and 88.8% at measured lower-5%, lower-10%, and lower-20% targets, respectively. Among 115 chemical–medium combinations meeting U.S. Environmental Protection Agency requirements, the lowest measured protective-apical threshold among panel members correlated with the full-data lower-5% benchmark (Spearman ρ = 0.847; 95% chemical-bootstrap interval, 0.756–0.904). None had measurements for all five members; 54 and 44 had measurements for one and two, respectively. Follow-up rankings for 639 chemicals depended on effect-family aggregation. Localized panels averaged 6.75 percentage points higher model-expected capture than the national panel across 32 states under matched weights; three data-limited states used the national panel. Deployment requires prospective assays, cultivation work, and matrix-specific validation.

Abstract Per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS) are contaminants of concern due to their persistence, occurrence in natural waters, and association with adverse health outcomes. Producing potable water from PFAS-impacted sources requires selectively removing PFAS from complex waters. Adsorptive membranes are an emerging strategy for PFAS removal due to their tunable architectures and chemistries, modularity, and high water permeances. However, it is difficult to compare adsorptive membrane performance across studies and identify membrane properties governing PFAS removal due to the diversity of materials, architectures, testing conditions, and reported performance metrics. This review critically evaluates the state of PFAS adsorptive membranes by examining nanofiber membranes, asymmetric membranes, adsorptive nanofiltration (NF) membranes, and ion exchange membranes used for adsorptive PFAS removal. We highlight structure-property-performance relationships, assess current testing strategies, and recommend standard performance metrics to enable cross-study comparisons. We further compare adsorptive membrane performance to conventional reverse osmosis (RO) and NF membranes. Finally, we apply the convection-diffusion-adsorption (CDA) model to published PFAS breakthrough data to gain mechanistic insights into the role of membrane properties and operating parameters on PFAS removal. Overall, this review provides a framework for evaluating adsorptive membranes, identifies key research gaps, and establishes design criteria to advance adsorptive PFAS separations.

articles.title:
Distinct Methane-Cycling
Pathways Drive Variable Surface
Flux in Freshwater Wetlands
articles.abstract: Abstract Freshwater wetlands are the largest natural source of methane (CH4), representing a third of global emissions. Both CH4 production and oxidation are microbially mediated, yet the metabolic controls governing CH4 cycling across wetland types remain poorly resolved. Here, we investigated six hydrologically and geochemically distinct wetlands in the Prairie Pothole Region of North America. By integrating genome-resolved metatranscriptomic data with porewater geochemistry, dissolved CH4 profiles, and chamber-based flux measurements across these wetlands, we assessed how microbial gene expression associated with electron acceptor utilization corresponds to CH4 cycling and identified the dominant methanogenic pathways driving CH4 production. CH4 porewater concentration varied across seasons and sites, with higher concentrations later in the season under more reducing conditions. Wetlands with higher expression of denitrification and sulfate reduction genes exhibited lower methanogenesis and porewater CH4 concentrations. Sites with higher porewater CH4 showed elevated expression of all three methanogenic pathways. Methanogenic activity, however, was not predictive of surface flux. Instead, emissions were modulated by site-specific physical and geochemical controls on methanotrophic CH4 consumption. These findings demonstrate that equivalent CH4 production can emerge through distinct microbial pathways, and that production alone is a poor predictor of atmospheric emissions. This distinction carries important implications for modeling wetland contributions to global CH4 budgets.
